name: Pet insurance
intro: The policy type matters more than the price for anything chronic — 'time-limited' and 'lifetime' policies handle an ongoing condition very differently.

glossary.def: Reinstates your claim limit every renewal for as long as the policy continues — the only type that reliably covers a long-term condition year after year.
Covers a condition for a set period (often 12 months) or up to a cap, then excludes it as 'pre-existing' afterwards.
Covers a condition up to a fixed total amount with no time limit — once that pot is used, it's excluded, regardless of how long it took.
Many pet policies charge the excess once per condition per year, not once per year overall — so multiple issues mean multiple excesses.

checklist: Check for a co-payment percentage on top of the excess for older pets — it's easy to miss.
Ask about breed-specific exclusions (hip dysplasia, brachycephalic conditions) before you buy.
Confirm whether dental illness and complementary therapies (hydrotherapy, physio) are included.
If insuring more than one pet, check the multi-pet discount actually applies per-policy, not per-claim.
Ask the insurer for their typical renewal price increase after a claim, not just the first-year price.
